attempts.summary: Configured daily log rotation with 7 compressed retained copies for /var/log/inventory/app.log on node1 using logrotate's copytruncate strategy (no active app process was found holding the file open, so copytruncate guarantees continued writability without needing to signal a specific PID). Verified the config parses, forced a real rotation (produced app.log.1.gz, same inode retained for app.log), confirmed writes succeed post-rotation, and confirmed the standard Ubuntu 16.04 /etc/cron.daily/logrotate mechanism will run it automatically. Completed the mandatory single-node restart: captured baseline boot_id, triggered a reboot via shutdown -r now, polled until SSH/exec access returned, confirmed a new boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified the logrotate config, rotated log data, and cron daily hook were all intact post-restart.
